title: When Validators and Repairs See the Same Candidate: A Confirmatory Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, paired experiment that evaluated a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The executed adapter used gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) with retrieval disabled (retrieval_augmented_generation = false) and exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded arms (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). On N = 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 judged every sampled initial candidate valid (250/250), no repairs were applied, and baseline and guarded final validity rates were identical (1.0). Mapping the preregistered estimand actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses required retrieval-augmented generation and were not testable in this execution; we document this preregistration deviation, quantify the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0), and discuss construct and external-validity limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, single deterministic validator, no RAG). All execution artifacts, preregistration, and analysis scripts are archived in the execution manifest.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and staged change workflows. Because LLM outputs can violate ordering constraints or operational invariants, guarded architectures combining generation with deterministic validators and bounded repairs (generate→validate→repair) are advocated to reduce actionable misconfigurations. We preregistered candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to test whether targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) increases actionable-misconfiguration rates. The executed run, however, used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation = false; consequently the empirical estimand realized by the run compares baseline single-shot validity of a shared sampled candidate versus the final guarded validity (validator ± permitted repair) on that same candidate. This paper (1) describes the preregistered design and the executed contract, (2) presents artifact-backed confirmatory results under the executed semantics, (3) documents the preregistration deviation that prevented testing RAG-poisoning, and (4) discusses implications and validity threats.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and application papers document active interest in LLM-driven NetOps including intent decomposition, intent-to-configuration translation, and zero-touch automation [1]–[5]. Prior work highlights hallucination and constraint violations as reliability threats that motivate tool-augmented or verifier-assisted architectures [6], [7]. Tool-augmented pipelines and RAG-style grounding have been proposed to improve factual grounding, but they introduce engineering tradeoffs and expose new attacker surfaces (e.g., poisoned retrieval fragments) discussed in adjacent-domain adversarial studies [8], [9]. Network verification and simulator tools (rule-based or formal) are common validator proposals for NetOps pipelines [10], yet systematic, topology-grounded measurements of guarded pipelines under adversarial retrievals remain an open gap motivating our preregistered experiment.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and executed contract: The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1. The frozen execution contract actually run declared adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; requested model = gpt-5-mini (provider openai_responses); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; retrieval_augmented_generation = false; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; task_count = 250. The manifest records model_configuration.temperature = null (unset); null/unset must not be interpreted as temperature = 0 or as evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was reused by both baseline and guarded arms; no independent per-condition sampling was performed. A constrained-prompt arm mentioned in the preregistration was not executed as an independent generation condition and therefore is not part of the realized estimand.

Tasks, validator, and estimand mapping: We used 250 deterministic synthetic intent→configuration tasks produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 produced the stored label VALID_CONFIGURATION (scorer value 1 indicates a valid, non-actionable configuration). To align preregistration and stored artifacts we operationalized actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION; this mapping is applied consistently in analysis and reporting.

Experimental flow and analysis: For each task the adapter requested one initial sample from the hosted model (shared across conditions). Baseline recorded the validator result on that initial candidate. Guarded executed the deterministic validator and, if violations were reported, permitted at most one repair attempt; the final guarded result recorded the validator status after any permitted repair. The primary confirmatory test was a paired comparison of actionable_misconfig indicators (exact McNemar two-sided test, α = 0.05). We also computed a paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Analysis used the registered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor operating on archived result files; all raw outputs, validator traces, and analysis code are archived in the execution bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting: The run completed (started 2026-08-31T21:04:12Z; completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56Z). Planned episodes 500 (2×250) completed with zero failed episodes; provider-call audit recorded 250 hosted-model call events corresponding to the shared initial generation stage. Representative artifacts show identical shared initial candidates across baseline and guarded arms for each pair.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed): Using stored scorer semantics (VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1) and the mapping actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION, the archived contingency table is n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (all 250 pairs had VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1). Thus actionable-misconfig counts are zero in both arms and the paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv) are archived and consistent with these results.

Preregistration deviation: The preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses required retrieval-augmented generation. The executed adapter had retrieval_augmented_generation = false and therefore injected no retrievals (poisoned or clean). This recorded deviation means the preregistered RAG/poisoning primary hypothesis was not testable in this run.
sections.discussion:
What the executed evidence supports: Under shared_initial_candidate semantics with a deterministic validator and retrieval disabled, the guarded pipeline did not change outcomes because the single sampled candidate reused across arms already satisfied validator checks for every task. The narrow, artifact-backed conclusion is: when baseline and guarded arms start from the same valid candidate (per deterministic_netops_validator_v5), the guarded pipeline produced no paired change in actionable-misconfiguration rate.

What it does not support: These results do not imply guarded pipelines are unnecessary in general. The experiment did not exercise retrieval-augmented generation, did not measure independent per-condition generation variability (by design), used synthetic tasks and one model/validator, and therefore cannot adjudicate the originally preregistered RAG-poisoning hypotheses or generalize across production topologies or alternative validators.

Power and assumption mismatch: The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline actionable-misconfig rate ≈ 0.05 and targeted detection of an absolute paired increase ≈ 0.05 with 80% power. The observed baseline actionable-misconfig rate was 0.0, violating that assumption and invalidating sensitive inference for the original poisoning hypothesis. The exact zero-event outcome produces tight CIs in this controlled corpus but does not provide evidence about RAG-enabled threat models.

Threats to validity: Internal validity — shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced and archived; this isolates validator/repair effects but precludes measuring independent-generation variability. Construct validity — the deterministic validator implements rule-based checks and may omit production failure modes (vendor-specific semantics, asynchronous state). External validity — synthetic task family, single LLM (gpt-5-mini), single deterministic validator, and disabled retrieval limit generalization. Conclusion validity — homogeneous outcomes produce precise within-run CIs that reflect the controlled corpus rather than operational heterogeneity.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; retrieval disabled). The run produced 250/250 VALID_CONFIGURATION outcomes, no repairs were applied, and no actionable misconfigurations were observed in either arm (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Crucially, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable because retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter; this preregistration deviation and the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0) limit confirmatory inference about retrieval-poisoning. Follow-up experiments that enable controlled retrieval augmentation and poisoning injection, broaden validator realism, and evaluate independent-generation semantics are necessary to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as a preregistration deviation.

The stored scorer semantics required explicit mapping to the preregistered estimand: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 corresponds to no actionable misconfiguration, hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This mapping was applied consistently in all reported analyses.

A single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
